scope: Five Warlord biome variants for capital supports/palace and provincial governor hall
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent modular biome-specific Warlord architecture atlas for a distant illustrated strategy map.
Use the reference as the architectural design and map-camera reference. Create a NEW sheet of FIFTEEN complete isolated parts in a FIVE-COLUMN by THREE-ROW grid, generous true-transparent gutters. No labels or drawn grid lines. Do not paint a whole city, region, landscape scene or ground tile. These are three architectural sections, each adapted to five biomes, to join other existing modular city sections.

CAMERA AND SCALE: all 15 parts use the reference's high diagonal three-quarter overhead camera, upper-left light, substantial roof/top planes and two wall faces. Tiny normal-size doors, windows and masonry bays; no giant toy-castle doorway. Retain the same building extent and detail scale between all five biome variants. Broad connected values, hard pixel clusters, selective dithering and restrained hatching; old-school dark fantasy. Slate/charcoal masonry, vermilion/brick-red roofs and cloth, oxidized teal bindings. Ossified ribs/spine braces are structural supports, not scattered bones. Inhabited and functional, repaired inner architecture, secondary outer decay. No visible people, readable or skull faces, eyes, text, UI, frames, crests or magical glow.

COLUMN ORDER LEFT TO RIGHT, repeated in all three rows:
1 PLAINS: architecture rests on shallow earthen foundations and worn grass margins, a few short roots/grass tufts at irregular feet. Open, relatively low material profile.
2 FOREST: living buttress roots clasp and thread through the lower architecture; mossy masonry, a few small branches/foliage clusters emerging from structural recesses. The building remains dominant and readable. No big surrounding forest painting.
3 ISLANDS: fitted sea-worn dark basalt foundation, a few salt-stained piers and restrained coastal scrub; the architecture visibly keys into low irregular rock ledges. No surrounding ocean rectangle, boat, beach scene or huge volcanic mountain.
4 SWAMP: raised masonry on short rib-braced timber/ossified pile supports and peat hummocks, dark wet lower stones, a few reeds and hanging moss. A short raised access end connects to the rest of the city. No lake backdrop or flat rectangular swamp plate.
5 MOUNTAINS: stepped bedrock retaining piers and low angular scree ledges merge with the architecture; rib-braced rock-cut access and a few wind-worn stone edges. Low fitted rocky foundation, not a giant standalone mountain.

ROW ORDER TOP TO BOTTOM:
ROW 1, five CAPITAL REAR FOUNDATION SECTIONS. Adapt the reference's rear terraced buttress section (reference cell 4): one LOW connected rear bank of several stone retaining piers, galleries and load-bearing ribs supporting a monumental citadel above. This is a foundation/support MODULE, no palace body, complete castle or summit towers. The biome interaction belongs to its irregular feet and supports; clear joining upper surfaces.
ROW 2, five CAPITAL UPPER PALACE SECTIONS. Adapt the reference's upper palace body (reference cell 6): one severe great hall with small lateral roof wings, many ordinary tiny windows, strong red roof plane and teal structural band. It attaches to a terrace below and the separate summit above. Biome roots, damp supports or rock-cut lower return walls are structurally integrated but restrained; do not bury the palace in scenery. Do not include the separate triple-prong crown summit.
ROW 3, five PROVINCIAL GOVERNOR HALL SECTIONS. Adapt the reference's governor hall (reference cell 9): a lower and broader red-roof administrative/assembly hall, attached small side wing and two squat buttressed corner bastions. Retain a legible usable ordinary entrance, no capital summit. Biome-specific foundation and walls visibly meet the building, rather than accessories scattered beside it. Only this principal hall section; gatehouse and gate court are separate pre-existing modules and must not be included.

Each part is complete, isolated and wholly inside its cell with wide true-alpha space, including rock/root projections and every roof tip. All fifteen share ONE consistent overhead diagonal projection. Preserve connection ends as construction interfaces. No arbitrary rectangular bases, painted regional contours, sky, scenic backdrops, giant tree/peak, fog or colour wash. Avoid uniform gold/cream edge outlines. Biome character comes from concrete architecture interacting with roots, terrain and moisture, not changing the entire building to a biome tint. True transparent background.
